My family has farmed this land for generations. We have about 8 mu. The soil here in Quzhou is loam — good for wheat and corn. Everyone around me grows winter wheat then summer corn, and I will do the same. That is what this land is suited for, what the markets expect, and what I know how to do.

For winter wheat, I will use the improved variety the village extension station recommended last year — most neighbors switched and their yields were decent. I will plough the field before planting, apply base fertilizer, and irrigate at jointing, heading, and grain fill. Three times is normal here. I will spray once or twice for aphids and rust if I see them.

For summer maize after the wheat harvest, I will buy hybrid seeds from the county seed shop — everyone uses hybrid now, you get much better yield. I will plant directly into the stubble with the rotary tiller, since it saves time and the landlord's son has a machine. Summer rain usually helps, so I only irrigate once or twice unless it is dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer in July.

I use a bit more fertilizer than maybe I should — my neighbor said I could cut back, but I worry about low yield. Better safe.
